A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same self-dialog PMD framework, Ego4D-PMD benchmark, and coherence metrics. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original VLM evaluations in Tables 1–2, human judgments and correlations in Appendix C, and supplementary experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 reports revised VLM evaluations, the human-study results, and additional rationale-free, diversity-ranking, and length-penalty experiments.

M1.justification: The principal self-dialog, NLI scoring, question selection, and DPO adapter procedures remain. Appendix E.9 adds a length-penalized generation variant, applying l = -1 during both training-data generation and inference to favor shorter questions.

E1.justification: The Ego4D-PMD data, domains, and mistake categories remain unchanged. Appendix E.5 adds a limited task extension: classification-only PMD, where models no longer must generate a supporting rationale. No additional dataset or domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds diversity-based question ranking for the three open VLMs and rationale-free decision baselines for all four VLMs, substantially extending the comparison beyond the existing self-dialog configurations. GPT-4o also joins the main test-set comparison; v1 already evaluated it on validation data, so it is not an entirely new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 replaces tuning the dialog cap over 2–10 iterations with fixing it at 10. DPO training-data generation changes from default stopping settings to selected settings, and training/inference hyperparameters and prompts are revised. These changes prevent interpreting the updated scores as same-setting improvements. One setting remains unclear: v2 Table 13 reports epsilon = 0.5 outside the stated search grid.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's human validation, training-data ablation, question-source analysis, and diagnostic cases, v2 adds targeted tests of removing rationales, replacing coherence ranking with semantic diversity, and penalizing question length (Appendices E.5, E.8, E.9). These investigate the value of rationales, alternative explanations for accuracy gains, and the suspected question-complexity problem. Existing ablations and several diagnostic examples are also revised.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly states that a random seed ensures equivalent ICL-example shuffling; v2 retains equivalent shuffling but drops the seed disclosure. The human-study Spearman correlation and significance-testing procedures remain unchanged, and neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for the main experiments. Changed coefficients and p-values are result changes.

E6.justification: Numerous main and appendix results change under revised settings: Table 1's LLaVA coherence-plus-ICL accuracy changes from 68.1% to 67.8%, while Table 2's likelihood-only DPO relevance changes from 94.5% to 75.7%. New results include GPT-4o test accuracy of 55.4% with rationales, 69.2% without rationales, and LLaVA diversity-plus-ICL accuracy of 67.1%. Appendix C's informativeness correlation changes from 0.32 to 0.33. The percentage-to-bits display conversion alone is not a result change.

T1.justification: The core NLI, relevance, informativeness, reference adjustment, and aggregation definitions are retained. Appendix E.9 adds the length-penalized beam-score definition p'_Q = p_Q / |Q|^l and its interpretation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain self-dialog PMD, the Ego4D-derived benchmark, NLI coherence metrics, and inference/fine-tuning interventions with different accuracy, coherence, and efficiency benefits. V2 foregrounds tradeoffs and renames explanations as rationales, but v1 already discusses these tradeoffs; the central scientific claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of the accuracy cost of rationales, semantic diversity as a partial explanation for gains, and the tradeoffs remaining under length penalties. The DPO training-data ablation is reinterpreted as largely comparable with or without ICL, replacing v1's lower-maxima conclusion. Section 8 also explicitly identifies NLI evaluator errors as limiting objectivity; the broader absence-of-ground-truth discussion was already present in v1 Appendix A.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses the human pilot's intermediate-output provenance, author/peer annotators, and LLaVA rephrasing, plus a 5% learning-rate warmup, linear decay, and minimum-validation-loss selection details. New controls include explicit prompts, model identification, and penalty settings. Conversely, Figure 6 loses its fixed-stopping-settings disclosure; this omission does not establish that those runs changed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around visual dialog, hallucination mitigation, iterative questioning, and newer reasoning models, including IdealGPT, SQ-LLaVA, clinical questioning, and fact verification. It adds PMD references such as Assembly101 and PREGO, and replaces the earlier physical-state ICL motivation with Coenen et al.'s human-inquiry perspective.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and systematically changes explainable PMD/explanations to coherent PMD/rationales. It moves VLM application details from Section 4.1 to Section 2.2, separates interventions from experimental results, reorganizes Appendix E, and extensively rewrites the introduction, results discussion, and related work.

P2.justification: V2 adds tables for training-data settings, rationale-free evaluation, diversity ranking, and length-penalty results, and expands the existing main comparison and DPO tables. Several Figure 7 example panels are replaced, while figures and tables are relocated and captions or labels revised. These substantially expand the visual evidence, although the overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important evaluation weaknesses by fixing the dialog cap for efficiency comparisons and adding rationale-free and diversity controls that test whether the claimed benefits require rationales or coherence scoring. The length-penalty experiment and clearer evaluator/pilot limitations further strengthen interpretation and transparency. These gains substantially improve the paper despite mixed performance outcomes and a remaining reproducibility inconsistency in Table 13's epsilon setting.
